issues.description: Field Farm.animals: The problem statement requires the Farm to hold its animals in a List and explicitly asks to implement it using an ArrayList and to initialize that ArrayList in the no-argument constructor. In the solution repository, the Farm class declares the field as 'private Queue<Animal> animals;' and initializes it with 'new LinkedList<>()', and the getter/setter in the solution use Queue<Animal>. This type mismatch (List/ArrayList in the spec vs Queue/LinkedList in the solution) changes the expected field type and the signatures of the getter/setter and can confuse students about the correct collection type to use and how addAnimal/iteration should behave.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent between the problem statement and the solution. Preferred fix: change the solution to use the List interface and an ArrayList implementation (e.g. 'private List<Animal> animals;' with 'this.animals = new ArrayList<>();' in the no-arg constructor), and update the getter/setter signatures to 'List<Animal>'. Update imports accordingly and ensure addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, and singFarmSong iterate over the List. Alternatively, if the Queue/LinkedList choice is intentional, update the problem statement to allow Queue/LinkedList and remove the ArrayList-specific instruction.
